exposure: type of clinician performing index Cesarean section (medical doctor vs. associate clinician)
outcome: mode of delivery of subsequent pregnancies
place of delivery of subsequent pregnancies
cohort: Women who had a Cesarean section at any of nine hospitals in Sierra Leone.
finding: Within 5 years after an index Cesarean section, approximately 27% of women became pregnant again, and among those attempting a trial of labor, 60.5% had a vaginal birth, with no significant difference in peripartum and long-term complications based on the type of clinician performing the index CS.
mod_finding: Among women who delivered after an index Cesarean section, 12% had a planned repeat CS, and of those attempting a trial of labor, 60.5% achieved a vaginal birth; significant differences in mode of birth were observed between wealth quintiles.
